subject: maths
card: I, V, X, L, C, D and M: read and write Roman numerals, including IV, IX, XL and years like MMXXVI.
title: Roman numerals
seo_title: Roman numerals practice for KS2: read and write I to M, IV, IX, XL and years
description: Free KS2 Roman numerals practice: the seven symbols, the rules for IV, IX, XL and XC, reading numbers to 1000 and writing years. Hints and worked answers for ages 8 to 11, plus a printable 1 to 100 chart.
intro: The Romans wrote numbers with letters. Learn the seven symbols and two simple rules, and you can read any Roman numeral, from clock faces to the year a film was made.

units.title: The seven symbols
units.blurb: I, V, X, L, C, D and M.

learn.p: **I** = 1, **V** = 5, **X** = 10, **L** = 50, **C** = 100, **D** = 500, **M** = 1000. A rhyme can help: I Value Xylophones Like Cows Do Milk.
When the symbols go from biggest to smallest, add them: VI = 5 + 1 = 6, XXII = 10 + 10 + 1 + 1 = 22, CL = 100 + 50 = 150.
You can repeat I, X, C and M up to three times in a row: III = 3, XXX = 30, CCC = 300. V, L and D are never repeated. There is no symbol for zero.

questions.hint: X is the symbol after V.
It is half of C, which is 100.
It comes between C (100) and M (1000).
questions.explain: D = 500. C is 100, M is 1000 and L is 50.

questions.hint: Biggest to smallest, so add: V + I + I.

units.title: IV, IX and taking away
units.blurb: A small symbol before a big one is taken away.

learn.p: If a smaller symbol comes **before** a bigger one, take it away. IV = 5 − 1 = 4. IX = 10 − 1 = 9.
There are only six: **IV** = 4, **IX** = 9, **XL** = 40, **XC** = 90, **CD** = 400, **CM** = 900. You only ever put I, X or C in front, and only before the next two symbols up.
XIV = X + IV = 10 + 4 = 14. XLIX = XL + IX = 40 + 9 = 49. Split the numeral into its parts, then add the parts.

questions.hint: I is before V, so take it away.
I is before X, so take it away.
X is before L, so take 10 away from 50.
X is before C, so take 10 away from 100.

questions.q: How do you write 19 in Roman numerals?
questions.explain: 19 = 10 + 9 = X + IX = XIX. XXI is 21, and XVIIII repeats I too many times.

units.title: Reading Roman numerals
units.blurb: Split it into parts, then add.

learn.p: Work from left to right. Look for the taking-away pairs (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM) and treat each pair as one part. Then add all the parts.
Films and buildings often show the year in Roman numerals. MMXXVI = 1000 + 1000 + 10 + 10 + 5 + 1 = 2026.

questions.q: A building has MDCCC carved over the door. What year is that?

learn.p: Split the number into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, write each part, then join them. 38 = 30 + 8 = XXX + VIII = XXXVIII.
49 is 40 + 9 = XL + IX = XLIX. It is **not** IL: you can only take I away from V or X.
Read your answer back and add it up. If you get the number you started with, it's right.

questions.q: How do you write 38 in Roman numerals?
How do you write 49 in Roman numerals?
questions.explain: 40 = XL and 9 = IX, so 49 = XLIX. IL isn't allowed, because I can only be taken away from V or X.
